label: AQ 0038
title: The tokenizer that was too simple

questions.q: Then why not a far bigger vocabulary, with whole sentences as tokens?
questions.a: Each token needs an embedding row and an output score, and rare tokens get few training examples. The BLT paper notes Llama 3 raised its average token from 3.7 to 4.4 bytes “at the cost of increasing the size of its embedding table 4x” over Llama 2.

teach.title: How it works: where the extra length costs

questions.q: Are there real advantages to bytes?
questions.a: Yes. The ByT5 paper found byte models “significantly more robust to noise” such as typos and better on spelling-sensitive tasks, the same weakness Day 66 shows with counting the r's in “strawberry”.

teach.title: How it works: where the extra length costs

questions.q: How do byte models fix the length problem?
questions.a: They shorten the sequence the big model sees. MEGABYTE cuts bytes into fixed patches with a small model inside each patch; Meta's BLT sizes patches by how predictable the next byte is, averaging 6 to 8 bytes, longer than Llama 3's 4.4-byte tokens.

teach.title: How it works: where the extra length costs

questions.q: A text is 4 times longer in bytes than in tokens. Roughly how much more attention work is it as bytes, and why?
questions.a: About 16 times, because each position scores every earlier one, so the number of scores grows with the square of the length. The rest of the model grows about 4 times.

teach.title: How it works: where the extra length costs

questions.q: Why isn't “bytes never hit an unknown token” a reason to drop BPE?
questions.a: Byte-level BPE, as in GPT-2, also starts from all 256 bytes, so it can encode any string; its merges just make common text shorter.

teach.title: How it works: where the extra length costs

questions.q: Why does a byte model make a Hindi sentence so much longer than its English version?
questions.a: Each Devanagari character takes 3 bytes in UTF-8, so Day 66's Hindi sentence is 89 bytes against 37 for the English. How much worse than BPE that is depends on the BPE: 5.7 times the attention scores in cl100k_base (English: 15.6 times), but 51 times in o200k_base.
